newsitem.title: JAPAN: China exchange says interested in option contracts.
newsitem.headline: China exchange says interested in option contracts.

text.p: Zhengzhou Commodity Exchange vice president Wang Xian Li said on Thursday that the exchange is interested in launching option contracts for agricultural commodities.
"The exchange has been considering listing options, and the discussions have been fruitful so far," he told reporters here.

"But the Chinese government is very cautious on this, and we would also like to think it over thoroughly before taking any action," Wang said. He is currently visiting Osaka, in western Japan, to exchange views and study derivatives trading with the Kansai Agricultural Commodities Exchange.

Asked whether the exchange is planning to launch a rice futures contract, Wang said: "Rice is already listed on two exchanges in southern China, where it is produced. We haven't yet taken action...in the north."
"But there is a possibility we may list it," he added.
The Zhengzhou exchange currently trades agricultural commodities such as wheat, corn and soymeal.
Its trade volume during the January-September period of this year totalled 32.74 million lots compared with 36.60 million for all of 1995.
